notes:
Inbound self-serve signup (trial) — small support SaaS focused on mid-market e-com merchants. Problem: EU customers report slow replies from the chat assistant (support bot). Customer quote: "Feels laggy for EU users — sometimes 2–3s end-to-end, drops conversation quality." They are on free tier; rate-limits and default timeouts suspected. Wants quick wins: region choice guidance, concrete timeout settings for SDKs, and recommendations for trimming prompts to reduce processing time and cost.

Key pain: perceived latency -> hurts user conversion. Cost sensitivity moderate (SMB) — willing to move to paid if stability/cost favorable. No hard compliance needs beyond SSO and audit logs. Tech stack: Node back-end, frontend in React, currently calling Redwood hosted API from us-east-1 (cloud provider defaults), many end-users in EU. Ask: how to shift to nearest region + best practice config to cut median and tail latency.

We recommended: 1) try eu-west-1 endpoint for EU traffic; 2) use SDK keepalive + connection pooling; 3) set conservative request timeout (connect 2s, read/overall 15s for non-streaming); 4) enable streaming responses for perceived latency improvement; 5) trim system prompts and do context window management (slot older messages into embeddings index and retrieve only top-K); 6) enable prefix caching for repeated system content; 7) set token budget per response (max_tokens ~ 256–512 depending on answer type). Added Optimize suggestions: quantization / smaller model variant for high-volume lower-cost paths, batch small requests, and TTL-based caching for repetitive queries.

Customer reaction: positive, asked for a short POC plan and a one-pager with exact timeout and SDK snippet. They also asked for a sample prompt-reduction checklist to hand to product team.

Quote from call: "If we can get p95 under 800ms for EU we can justify a paid plan."
